content: 1. Monitor health and immunization programs to identify community needs and collaborate with communities to address those needs effectively. 2. Conduct operational and social science research to determine successful strategies for reducing inequalities and improving the quality and delivery of immunization services. 3. Develop and implement new strategies to address inequities in immunization coverage and ensure that global vaccine programs, particularly those focusing on eradication and elimination goals, are integrated into national immunization programs. 4. Ensure that the deployment of new vaccines is accompanied by comprehensive disease-control plans. 5. Facilitate coordination between public and private sectors for the introduction of new vaccines, reporting of vaccine-preventable diseases, and administration of vaccines, while maintaining high-quality vaccination standards in both sectors. 6. Consider incorporating vaccines into health programs across the life course to ensure comprehensive immunization coverage. 7. Strengthen monitoring and surveillance systems to improve the quality of immunization administrative data and promote its analysis and use at all administrative levels to enhance program performance. 8. Develop and promote the use of new technologies for the collection, transmission, and analysis of immunization data. 9. Further strengthen, improve the quality of, and expand disease surveillance systems to generate laboratory-confirmed case data for decision-making, monitor the impact of immunization on morbidity and mortality, and track changes in disease epidemiology. 10. Ensure capacity for vaccine safety activities, including the ability to collect and interpret safety data, with enhanced capacity in countries introducing newly developed vaccines. 11. Strengthen the capacity of managers and frontline workers to ensure that immunization and other primary healthcare programs have adequate human resources to deliver predictable, high-quality services. 12. Increase levels of pre-service, in-service, and post-service training for healthcare personnel, and develop new, relevant curricula that integrate immunization as a component of comprehensive disease control. 13. Promote coordinated training and supervision of community-based health workers to enhance their effectiveness in delivering immunization services. 14. Innovate to improve cold-chain capacity, logistics, and waste management systems to ensure the safe storage and transportation of vaccines. 15. Minimize the environmental impact of energy, materials, and processes used in immunization supply systems, both within countries and globally. 16. Staff immunization supply systems with adequate numbers of competent, motivated, and empowered personnel at all levels. 17. Establish information systems that enable staff to accurately track the availability of vaccine supplies. 18. Advocate for governments to invest in immunization programs according to their financial capacity and the expected benefits, while engaging new potential domestic and development partners to diversify funding sources. 19. Develop innovative financing mechanisms to increase the affordability of vaccines, particularly for middle-income countries, and explore differential pricing approaches to define explicit criteria for price tiers. 20. Strengthen budgeting and financial management within countries to better integrate financial and healthcare planning and priority setting. 21. Coordinate funding support from development partners and other external sources, and evaluate funding mechanisms based on their effectiveness in achieving disease-control goals. 22. Build and support networks of regulators and suppliers to share best practices and improve quality assurance and control capabilities. 23. Develop tools to strengthen global standardization of manufacturing and regulatory processes, and harmonize national regulatory systems with globally aligned regulations. 24. Engage with end-users to prioritize vaccines and innovations based on perceived demand and added value, and establish platforms for exchanging information on immunization research and consensus building. 25. Build capacity and human resources in lowand middle-income countries to conduct research and development (R&D) and operational research, while fostering partnerships among institutions in high-, middle-, and low-income countries. 26. Promote collaboration between traditional research disciplines and scientists from fields not previously engaged in vaccine research to drive innovation. 27. Conduct research on the fundamentals of innate and adaptive immune responses in humans, as well as the immunologic and molecular characteristics of microbes, to enable the development of new vaccines. 28. Accelerate the development, licensing, and uptake of vaccines by promoting access to technology, know-how, and intellectual property for adjuvants and their formulation into vaccines. 29. Develop non-syringe delivery mechanisms and vaccine packaging tailored to the needs and constraints of national immunization programs. 30. Research the use of modern communication technologies to disseminate more effective information about immunization programs. 31. Conduct representative epidemiological, immunological, social, and operational studies to evaluate vaccine impact and guide health economics analysis. 32. Perform operational research to improve delivery approaches for life-course immunization and vaccination in humanitarian emergencies, fragile states, and conflict-affected regions. 33. Develop improved diagnostic tools for conducting disease surveillance in low-income countries to enhance immunization program effectiveness.
